key_insight: Dense, fine-lamellar Fe-based amorphous coatings favor long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray parameters and service humidity should inform coating design for corrosion and wear protection of Q235 carbon steel.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Examine droplet morphology, coating microstructure, and porosity.
Evaluate corrosion and sliding wear against Si3N4 balls under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract links higher porosity to poorer long-term corrosion resistance and reports decreasing friction coefficients and wear rates with increasing humidity.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical performance values or humidity ranges, and the wear trends may depend on the Si3N4 counterface.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
